title: Brake Pads
intro: You brake with your ankle and your calf. When the ankle won't let your knee travel forward, you can end up pulling up high instead of sitting into the last step, and the push back out of the corner gets slower. So we open up the ankle first, then build the calf to hold that range.
Do it after training or on its own day. You need a step or the bottom stair, and a wall to hold onto. No step works too, you just lose the stretch at the bottom. An easy bike does the walk's job.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: A stiff ankle, not an injured one. If a knee, an Achilles or an ankle is sore rather than stiff, someone should look at you first, and then the knee, Achilles and ankle session in the Care list is the one built for it.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: If you've rolled it lately, it's swollen, it gives way, your knee hurts in the deep position, you felt a pop or a snap at the back of the ankle or calf, you get a sharp spot in the calf or Achilles, or the tendon itself is sore and it's worse the next morning.

before.label: Swollen calf
before.text: If one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing, see a doctor the same day.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: It leaves your calves tired for a day or two. Keep it two days clear of a match and of braking work on court.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do two sets of each loaded exercise and see how you feel in two days.

good: Walk at an easy pace and roll through each foot
Feel your calves and ankles warming up

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rocks
exercises.note: A doorframe works if you don't have a wall to face.

good: Drive the knee forward over your toes with your heel down
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting your heel lift to get the knee further

good: Lean back against a wall with your feet a step out and lift your toes toward your shins
Feel the muscle along the front of your shin
bad: Bending at the hips to help the lift

good: Walk on the balls of your feet with your heels high
Feel your calves and the arches of your feet working
bad: Letting your heels sink between steps

good: From downward dog, bend one knee and press the other heel toward the floor
Feel the stretch through the calf and Achilles of the straight leg
bad: Rounding your back to reach the heel down

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.note: This is one long hold, not reps, and if the front of the ankle pinches rather than stretches, take the knee back a little.

good: Sink into a long split stance and drive the front knee forward over your toes
Feel the front ankle stretch and the thigh working

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.note: 3s lower. Lower until your heels are just below the step, and if the last set feels easy, wear a backpack with a couple of books in it.

good: Rise onto the balls of both feet from the edge of a step, holding a wall, then take three seconds to lower
Feel the calves working the whole way down
Keep your knees bent and stay there as you rise onto the balls of your feet
Feel the deeper calf muscle under the big one working
bad: Straightening your knees as you rise
